pattern.crimePattern: courier kills a craftsman who refused to finish a forged seal
pattern.notes: Fictional print shop, courier company and shell company. River Road is a setting only. Opens the spine story.

ob.reportedBy: Juma Mwakio, apprentice, Omar Printers & Rubber Stamps
ob.text: Apprentice Juma Mwakio reports that his employer, Rashid Omar Bakari (56), owner of Omar Printers & Rubber Stamps, River Road, was found dead in the back room of the shop at 19:40. Drawers ransacked. A customer was seen shouting at the deceased in the street earlier in the evening.

people.name: Rashid Omar Bakari
people.occupation: Printer and rubber-stamp maker, Omar Printers
people.bio: Thirty years on River Road. Makes every rubber stamp in the street worth having. Writes down the ID number of anyone who collects an official-looking stamp.

image.brief: Kenyan Swahili man, mid 50s, white kofia, trimmed grey beard, ink-stained fingers, reading glasses on his nose, a rubber stamp in one hand, dignified and stubborn, ID-photo framing

people.name: Tom Ochieng
people.bio: Rides for Haraka Couriers in a yellow rain jacket. Appears in no customer list: only on a carbon collection slip.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 30s, yellow courier rain jacket with HARAKA COURIERS on the chest, a helmet under his arm, blank careful expression, photographed against a police height chart as an arrest photo

people.name: Hillary Kosgei
people.bio: His wedding cards were misprinted. He shouted at Rashid in front of the whole street at 17:00.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, wedding-season haircut, a box of misprinted invitation cards under his arm, angry and embarrassed, ID-photo framing

people.name: Elizabeth Achola
people.occupation: Owner of the print shop next door
people.bio: Her shop shares a wall with Rashid's. They've been fighting about the rent the landlord splits between them.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, late 40s, printer's apron over a smart dress, reading glasses on a chain, a stack of fresh prints in her hands, sharp but fair face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Juma Mwakio
people.bio: Learning the trade. Was out delivering wedding cards in Ngara. Found the body.

image.brief: Kenyan teenager, 19, ink on his fingers and a smear on his cheek, oversized shop coat, devastated, ID-photo framing

people.name: Abdullahi Gure
people.occupation: Night askari for the row of shops
people.bio: Walks the River Road shopfronts from 18:00 with a rungu and a torch.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 60s, white stubble, a heavy army-green greatcoat with plain buttons, a knitted cap, a torch held at his chest, alert old eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Zuhura Mwakio (Mama Juma)
people.bio: Her neighbour's daughter is getting married; Juma brought the cards.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 40s, a black buibui with a patterned headscarf, a cream wedding-invitation card held in her hand, anxious, ID-photo framing

places.name: Haraka Couriers depot, Tom Mboya Street

locations.name: Omar Printers & Rubber Stamps, River Road
locations.description: Friday evening on River Road: printing shops, sign-writers and stamp-makers, all lit, all busy. Omar Printers has a front counter, an order book, a carbon collection-slip book, and a back room with a stamp-making bench and a wall of labelled drawers. Every drawer has been pulled out.

hotspots.label: Back room, by the stamp bench
hotspots.text: Rashid lies by his stamp bench. The handle of the stamp press is on the floor. Every drawer on the wall has been pulled out and tipped. Under the counter, the cash box is closed.

hotspots.label: One drawer on the floor
hotspots.text: Most drawers were pulled out and spilled. This one was emptied: not a single blank or proof left. Its label: 'Mvua — Friday'.

hotspots.label: Order book on the counter
hotspots.text: Rashid's order book: every job, client, deposit and collection date.

hotspots.label: Under the order book
hotspots.text: A carbon-paper collection-slip book. The top copy has been torn out. The carbon copy beneath is still there.

hotspots.label: Tucked inside the order book
hotspots.text: A plain white card, slipped between two pages as a bookmark.

hotspots.label: River Road outside
hotspots.text: The night askari, Abdullahi Gure, leans on his rungu at the corner.

hotspots.label: Achola Prints next door
hotspots.text: Elizabeth Achola's shop is still serving. She hands over her carbon receipt book before she's asked.

image.brief: River Road in Nairobi on a Friday night, narrow street of printing and rubber-stamp shops lit by bare bulbs and signage, sign-writers' boards, a small print shop with its shutter half down, no people in focus

body.note: Report language only. Struck with the stamp-press handle. Drawers ransacked. Cash box untouched under the counter: KSh 18,400.

facts.text: Rashid Omar Bakari was found dead in the back room of Omar Printers at 19:40.
A customer, Hillary Kosgei, shouted at Rashid in the street earlier in the evening.
Rashid was struck with the handle of his stamp press.
Every drawer was pulled out, but the cash box under the counter is untouched: KSh 18,400.
Only one drawer was completely emptied: the one labelled 'Mvua — Friday'.
Order book: 'Replica seal — REGISTRAR OF TITLES — client: Mvua Holdings — deposit by Till 880 214 — collect Fri 19:00 by messenger.'
The month's other clients (Kilele House Management, St. Teresa's Church, Tana Express, H. Kosgei) had ordinary jobs already collected or not due tonight.
Carbon slip: 'Mvua order. Collector: Tom Ochieng, Haraka Couriers. 19:02 — REFUSED. Told him I won't finish it.'
A card in the order book: 'Kivuli wants it Friday. No excuses.'
At about 19:20 a man in a yellow Haraka Couriers rain jacket came out of Omar Printers with a brown envelope and walked fast towards Tom Mboya Street.
Abdullahi: Hillary Kosgei shouted at Rashid at 17:00 and left. The whole street saw.
Abdullahi was on his rounds along the shopfronts all evening.
Achola Prints sold to customers at 19:00, 19:08, 19:14 and 19:20, with people waiting the whole time.
Elizabeth's customers saw Abdullahi pass on his rounds at 19:08 and 19:14.
Juma's delivery note: wedding cards to Z. Mwakio, Ngara, signed 19:15.
Mama Juma: Juma arrived in Ngara at 18:50 and stayed for tea until 19:30.
Hillary's coach ticket: Nairobi–Eldoret, departed 17:45. He's calling from Nakuru.
Juma: Rashid and Elizabeth Achola next door have been fighting about the rent split for months.
Juma: Rashid said this week, 'That Mvua job is not a stamp. It's a key to other people's land.'
Juma: Rashid always wrote down the name and ID of anyone collecting an official-looking stamp.
Hillary: "I shouted, yes. My wedding is in two weeks. Then I went to the coach."
Elizabeth: "We fought about rent like neighbours do. I was serving all evening."
Juma: "I was in Ngara with the cards. I came back at twenty to eight and found him."

interrogations.intro: Juma sits on the shop step with his hands black with ink. "He taught me to cut letters backwards. Backwards, so they print the right way."

topics.reply: He wrote down the ID of anyone who collected a stamp that looked official. Every time. He said a stamp is a promise.
Mvua. That job made him angry all week. He said, 'That's not a stamp, Juma. It's a key to other people's land.'
Mama Achola next door? They fight about rent every month. But she brings him tea when he's working late.
Call my mother. I was there with the cards, having tea.

interrogations.intro: Abdullahi taps his rungu on the kerb. "I walk this row every night. I know every door on it."

topics.reply: The wedding man shouted at five and went off with his box. He didn't come back.
Yellow jacket. Haraka. Twenty past seven, out of Rashid's door with a brown envelope, walking fast. I thought, a late delivery.

interrogations.intro: Elizabeth keeps one hand on her receipt book. "We fought about rent. I'd never hurt him. Here is every sale I made tonight."

topics.reply: He was a stubborn old goat and the best stamp fundi on this road. Who will cut my stamps now?

interrogations.intro: Hillary, by phone from Nakuru, over bus noise: "Dead? I shouted at him about my cards. My God."

topics.reply: He promised me a free reprint on Monday. I was rude to him. I'll have to live with that.

interrogations.intro: Haraka Couriers' depot. Tom Ochieng hangs up his yellow jacket very slowly when Amani says the shop's name.

topics.reply: I collect what I'm sent to collect.

chargeSheet.template: {who} killed {victim} when he refused to finish a stamp ordered by {client}.

prosecutor.pass: Ochieng carried it out. But he didn't order it. Who is Mvua Holdings?
fail: This doesn't hold up. A courier doesn't kill over a parcel unless someone is waiting for it. Look again.
No. Both names have to be right. Who came at seven, and for whose order?

proof.concludes: The robbery was staged: the cash was left, and the only drawer actually emptied was the Mvua order.
The Mvua order was due for collection at 19:00. The collector who came at 19:02 and was refused was Tom Ochieng of Haraka Couriers.
A man in a Haraka jacket left at 19:20 with an envelope, between the refusal and the body being found. Tom Ochieng killed Rashid for Mvua Holdings' order.

eliminations.why: Hillary was on the 17:45 coach to Eldoret.
Elizabeth was serving customers next door at 19:00, 19:08, 19:14 and 19:20.
Juma was in Ngara from 18:50 to 19:30 with the cards.
Abdullahi was seen on his rounds by Elizabeth's customers at 19:08 and 19:14.
Kilele House's office stamp was collected on Tuesday.
St. Teresa's stamp was collected on Monday.
Tana Express's stamps aren't due until next Wednesday.

reconstruction.text: Three weeks ago a client calling itself Mvua Holdings pays a deposit by PesaPap for a 'replica' seal: REGISTRAR OF TITLES.
Rashid cuts the blank, then looks closely at the proof. It's for forging land titles. He refuses to finish it.
19:02. A courier in a yellow Haraka jacket comes to collect. Rashid writes down his name and ID, then 'REFUSED'. The courier has orders not to leave without it.
In the back room the courier strikes Rashid with the stamp-press handle, empties the Mvua drawer and pulls out every other drawer to make it look like thieves.
He leaves at 19:20 with a brown envelope. He misses two things: the carbon copy of the slip, and a card in the order book with a name on it.

afterVerdict.beat: Tom Ochieng, arrested at the Haraka depot, says one word to Amani: "Kivuli." Then nothing.

The Pattern File unlocks: a second corkboard on the wall. Three pins are already on it: Till 880 214 from this case, the Mvua calendar from case 6 with the same till, and the card 'Kivuli wants it Friday'.
Mwalimu's voice-note: "You've seen that number before. Write it down somewhere I can't see it."
Collectible: Juma gives Amani Rashid's brass shop stamp, 'Omar Printers — River Road'. It stamps every charge sheet from now on.

tier1.line: Rashid wrote down everyone who collected official stamps. Look under the order book.

tier2.line: A courier refused at 19:02, and a courier's jacket leaving at 19:20. Then ask whose order he came for.

glossary.def: Wooden club carried by watchmen and herders.
Embroidered cap, often worn by Muslim men.
Fictional mobile-money service used in the game.

ui.beatNotes: Two blanks in one group (preparing for multi-group sheets). After the verdict: the Pattern File unlocks with three pins, and the desk collectible system starts with Rashid's stamp.
